nodes.summary: Over the three-letter alphabet $\{a, b, c\}$ (the letters $0, 1, 2$), the language of the words $a^n b^n c^n$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$ is not context-free.
nodes.title: The language $a^n b^n c^n$ is not context-free

nodes.summary: Over the three-letter alphabet $\{a, b, c\}$ (the letters $0, 1, 2$), this is the language of the words $a^n b^n c^n$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$: $n$ copies of $a$, then $n$ copies of $b$, then $n$ copies of $c$.
nodes.title: The language $a^n b^n c^n$

nodes.summary: For letters $a$ and $b$ of an alphabet with decidable equality, the language of the context-free grammar with a single nonterminal $S$, its start symbol, and the two rules $S \to aSb$ and $S \to \varepsilon$ is the language of the words $a^n b^n$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: The grammar $S \to aSb \mid \varepsilon$ generates $a^n b^n$

nodes.summary: For letters $a$ and $b$ of an alphabet with decidable equality, this is the context-free grammar with a single nonterminal $S$, which is its start symbol, and the two rules $S \to aSb$ and $S \to \varepsilon$.
nodes.title: The grammar $S \to aSb \mid \varepsilon$

nodes.summary: For any alphabet and any letters $a$ and $b$ of it, the language of the words $a^n b^n$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$ is context-free.
nodes.title: The language $a^n b^n$ is context-free

nodes.summary: For letters $a$ and $b$ of an alphabet, this is the language of the words $a^n b^n$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$: $n$ copies of $a$ followed by $n$ copies of $b$.
nodes.title: The language $a^n b^n$

nodes.summary: There is a context-free language $L$ over the three-letter alphabet $\{0, 1, 2\}$ whose complement is not context-free.
nodes.title: Context-free languages are not closed under complement

nodes.summary: There are context-free languages $L$ and $M$ over the three-letter alphabet $\{0, 1, 2\}$ whose intersection $L \cap M$ is not context-free.
nodes.title: Context-free languages are not closed under intersection

nodes.summary: For a letter $a$ of an alphabet, a word $w$ belongs to the Kleene star of the language $\{a\}$ whose only word is the one-letter word $a$ if and only if $w = a^k$ for some $k \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: The Kleene star of a one-letter word

nodes.summary: It is not the case that for every context-free language $L$ over the three-letter alphabet $\{0, 1, 2\}$, the complement of $L$ is context-free.
nodes.title: Complements of context-free languages need not be context-free

nodes.summary: Over the three-letter alphabet $\{0, 1, 2\}$, it is not the case that for all context-free languages $L$ and $M$ the intersection $L \cap M$ is context-free.
nodes.title: Intersections of context-free languages need not be context-free

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
